newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank sets guidelines on Europeso.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank sets guidelines on Europeso.

text.p: The Philippine Monetary Board has cleared the way for Europeso bonds with the approval of guidelines on sale of such instruments, the Central Bank said on Monday.
The guidelines said prior Central Bank approval would be needed for the issuance of such notes and their subsequent exchange for pesos to the local banking system.
The import or export of the Philippine currency is prohibited "whether physically or electronically," the statement said.
In case of multilateral agencies which want to issue peso-denominated instruments, prior approval would be needed from the Department of Finance, the statement said.

The Central Bank said five underwriters have so far indicated their willingness to arrange a maiden Europeso note. They are: ING Barings, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Merrill Lynch, Bank of Tokyo and Citibank.
Two multilateral institutions have also showed their willingness to issue the first Europeso note, the Central Bank said.
In a separate announcement, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said the bank was looking at launching 30-year and 100-year Yankee bonds in late April or May.
He said the Central Bank may choose the underwriters in the next two weeks.

A total of 12 groups have so far proposed the Yankee bonds. They are: JP Morgan, Citicorp, Morgan Stanley, ING Baring, CS First Boston, Goldman Sachs, Lehman Brothers, Salomon Brothers, Bankers' Trust, Merrill Lynch, Deustche Morgan Grenfell and Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp.
The Philippine government has so far issued dollar bonds in the Euromarket and yen-denominated bonds in the Japanese market.
